summary: We have developed an SI-powered dashboard, separating the science of combustion in microgravity into five core research areas: understanding, prevention, detection, suppression, and application. We aim to educate users on the science and allow them to access topical and relevant research tailored to their needs. Additionally, the site features an SI assistant that can clear up any confusion a user might have. The site also allows a user to compare and evaluate different methods of prevention, detection, suppression etc, according to their needs and priorities.
details:
Project Details

Our project is an interactive website, coded using the help of SI tools such as GPT Astra and Codex. We aim to explore how microgravity affects fire safety in space. Our project contains many simulations of the concepts mentioned, such as ventilation, the formation of cool flame, and smoke detection. Our aim was to take these complex ideas, which can be obtuse at times for students to understand and interpret, and transform them into demos, that allow for users to intuitively understand these concepts, as we mention below in our priorities. Along with the demos, our project features an SI intelligence, available in the Bottom right of the screen, which is available to break down and explain any concepts a user needs help with. Additionally, our project compares the different approaches to fire safety and evaluates each project and ranking them according to a set of criteria. For example we rank the three types of detector by particle coverage, power consumption, durability, and detection sensitivity.

Accuracy:  We wanted our research to as accurate as possible, so we did extensive research into the topics of choice. Additionally, on our site, those who wish to learn more about the project are able to find sources, and prompts for further research, at the bottom of every page.

Accessibility / User experience:  We wanted our project to be digestible and accessible for all, so we included interactive demonstrations of the complex scientific concepts our project touches on, such as the formation of cool flame, allowing for users to play around with the concepts – giving the user a deeper understanding than if they were to just read blocks of dense text.

Real world relevance:  We feel that it is important that those using our project understand that this research is not just applicable to space travel but can have applications on earth too. To show this we designed the Applications tab of our website to illustrate these uses. This includes finding fire-safe materials, the theoretical potential of cool flames, and historical developments, such as improving the suits of firefighters.
